round.name: Election Night: How US Elections Work

questions.q: Let's start with the big room: how many voting seats are there in the US House of Representatives?
Members of the House face the voters again pretty quickly. How long is one House term?
The 26th Amendment, ratified in 1971, lowered the minimum voting age in the United States from 21 to what?
Senators serve staggered terms. Roughly what fraction of the Senate's seats is up for election every two years?
There are 538 electoral votes in the Electoral College. How many does a candidate need to win the presidency outright?
Ratified in 1920, which numbered amendment to the US Constitution barred states from denying the vote on account of sex?
What is the minimum age to serve as a member of the US House of Representatives?
House seats are shared out among the states again every ten years, based on the results of what national count?
Before 1913, US senators were chosen by state legislatures. Which numbered amendment gave that choice directly to the voters?
In what year did Congress pass the law setting one nationwide day, the Tuesday after the first Monday in November, for choosing presidential electors?
